passage:
The school hall in Bergen was packed for the final of the five-a-side. Freya ran onto the last pass with her tongue between her teeth, the goal wide open, and kicked the ball high over the bar. The whole hall groaned, then someone laughed, then more. Her face burned and she stared at her boots.
Alejandro, the goalkeeper on the other team, jogged over. "That's the highest ball I've ever seen," he said, grinning, "and I still nearly dived." Freya snorted despite herself.
On the bus home she kept replaying it. By Monday two other people had fumbled something worse, and nobody mentioned her miss. At Tuesday practice she asked the coach to set up the same pass again.

qa.q: Where did Freya miss the goal?
qa.a: She missed in the school hall in Bergen, during the final of the five-a-side.

qa.q: What was Freya feeling right after the laughter began?
qa.a: She felt embarrassed and ashamed: her face burned and she stared at her boots.

qa.q: What helped Freya move on from the miss?
qa.a: Alejandro's joke let her laugh a little, time passed, and she went back to practise the same pass again.

qa.q: How might Alejandro have seen Freya's miss?
qa.a: He saw it as a funny, harmless moment, so he joked kindly with her instead of laughing at her.

grounding: A teen fails in front of everyone and is laughed at; shame fades faster than expected, she laughs and tries again.

passage:
Dear Dhruv,
You'll laugh, but I'm writing an actual letter because Mom says I text like a robot.
So, annual day. I was supposed to recite the long Hindi poem. I got to the second verse and my brain just emptied. Nothing. I stood there with hundreds of parents watching for about ten seconds, which felt like ten years, and then some boys in the back row started laughing. I walked off and cried in the washroom. Not ashamed to tell you.
Here's the weird part. By Monday, nobody cared. Two people did a squeaky 'uhhh' impression at me, and I actually laughed and did it back, louder. They got bored.
Ms Kapoor asked if I wanted to recite at the Hindi Diwas assembly next month. I said yes before I could chicken out. I'm practising in front of Mom, the mirror and probably the cat.
If I freeze again, I'll just say 'one second, rebooting' 😅
Sumit

qa.q: Where did Sumit go after walking off stage?
How was Sumit feeling while standing frozen on stage?
qa.a: Sumit felt panicked and humiliated; ten seconds felt like ten years as the back row laughed.

qa.q: What helped the laughter die down?
qa.a: Laughing at the 'uhhh' impression and doing it back louder, so the teasing lost its fun.

qa.q: How does Ms Kapoor see Sumit after the freeze?
qa.a: She still believes in Sumit, offering another chance to recite at the next assembly 🙂

grounding: A letter from a teen who froze on stage and was laughed at, finding the shame faded fast, laughing it off and agreeing to try again.

passage: Okay, Hafsa, since you keep asking, I'll tell the penalty story. I'm Nilesh, school team, number 9, famous for one thing now. Inter-school final, last minute, we get a penalty. Coach points at me. The whole school's on the stands. I run up, slip on the wet grass, and the ball goes about two metres, rolling, straight into the keeper's hands. Everyone howled. By evening somebody had made it a sticker in the class group. I didn't sleep that night. I thought I'd have to change schools. But here's what I didn't expect: by Wednesday, people had moved on to someone's haircut. On Friday I sent the sticker to the group myself with 'my best work 🙂'. Even the other team laughed with me. Then I stayed back after every practice, taking penalties till dark. First match next season, I scored one. You were there. You screamed louder than my mum.

qa.q: What happened when Nilesh took the penalty?
qa.a: Nilesh slipped on the wet grass and the ball rolled about two metres into the keeper's hands.

qa.q: What was Nilesh feeling the night after the final?
qa.a: Nilesh felt so ashamed and humiliated that changing schools seemed like the only way out.

qa.q: What did Nilesh do that turned the mockery around?
qa.a: Sent the sticker to the group with 'my best work', laughing at it, then practised penalties until scoring one next season.

qa.q: How did Hafsa react to the goal next season?
qa.a: Hafsa was thrilled, screaming louder than Nilesh's mum.

grounding: A spoken account of a teen who missed a penalty and was laughed at, learning the shame faded fast, laughing at it and trying again.
